messages.body_plain:
Hi Mateusz,

Just realized that fragpipe msstats input doesn't have to go through a converter, while using dataProcess function, it's still affected by remove few measurements action (Features with one or two measurements across runs are removed). It results in proteins with two peptides faithfully quantified in both replicates of one condition but none in the two replicates of control got filtered out. Do you have any suggestion or fix on this issue?

Best,
Weixian

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

These warnings actually come from the missing value imputation (MBimpute=TRUE in the parameters). We fit the missing values with the survreg.fit function, and if the function fails to converge then you will see this warning. This generally happens when we do not have enough information to impute. In cases where the model does not converge, you should see those values left NA. I've run your data and the imputed values look generally reasonable as far as I can tell. As such I think you are ok to ignore these warnings.

In general with missing value imputation I would always recommend taking a closer look at the imputed values using profile plots to ensure that they make sense.

Best,
Devon

>

Then I wrote an entire description of each sample into a single text in the "Conditions" column. For example: "Cell.TreatA.2hrs". The annotation file is attached.
>
> When running MSstats, the FittedModels are "lm(formula = ABUNDANCE ~ GROUP, data = input)", which does not account for any paired comparisons.
>
> Are there any extra columns that I would be able to add to pass extra information to MSstats? Or should I use another method other than MSstats?
>
> Best,
> Luiz
